JUDGMENT:
1. This Judgment shall decide the instant appeal filed by the appellant/Food Business Operator(FBO) purportedly under Section 76 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 as amended upto date (hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act') assailing impugned order dated 19.04.2022 passed by Sh. Nagendra Shekhar Pati Tripathi, Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (Central), whereby the appellant has been held guilty of violating various provisions of the Act and the Regulations framed thereunder for selling "Cow Desi Ghee", the sample of which was found to be "misbranded".

BRIEF FACTS:
2. Briefly stated, on 16.01.2020, Sh. Naresh Kumar Sharma, the Food Safety Officer (in short "FSO")
visited M/s Bankey Bihari Dairy, A Unit of Bankey Bihari Trading Co., where he met the FBO,
Smt. Bhavna Gupta vs The State on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65674291/
1
namely Smt. Bhavana Gupta, W/o Sh. Anil Kumar Gupta and he identified himself and discloses his intention for taking sample of "Cow Desi Ghee" for analysis

. It is stated that no public witness came forward but Sh. Anil Kumar, Process Server was joined as a witness to the proceedings and at about 3:35pm, samples of "Cow Desi Ghee", which was meant for human consumption and being sold from the aforesaid address were taken; and that the sample consisted of four plastic jars, each containing 500 grams of "Cow Desi Ghee"
(ready for sale for human consumption) as originally sealed and capped plastic jars by the FBO bearing no label declaration but disclosed to be of the same batch to the FSO and that each plastic jar containing the sample was marked, packed, fastened and sealed as per the prescribed procedure and the signatures of the FBO were obtained vide prescribed Form VA and Panchnama was done at the spot and a sum of Rs.1400/ was paid towards the cost of four plastic jars, each containing 500 grams of "Cow Desi Ghee".

It was the case of the department that on 17.01.2020, one part of the aforesaid sample of "Cow Desi Ghee" bearing sample code number 128/1054/11/2020 with Designated Officer Code number 01/DO20/15667 in intact condition along with copy of memo in Form VI under a sealed packet along with another copy of memo in Form VI under sealed cover were sent separately to the Food Analyst, Delhi.

3. To cut the long story short, the Food Analyst vide its report bearing No. FSS/182/2020 dated 27.01.2020 reported and opined that the sample was 'misbranded' because there was violation of Regulation 2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.1, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.6, 2.2.2.7, 2.2.2.8, 2.2.2.9 & 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety &
Standards (Packaging & Labelling) Regulation, 2011 (in short "FSS (P&L) Regulation).
A copy of the Food Analyst Report was sent to the FBOcumProprietor Smt. Bhavana Gupta on 04.02.2020.

As per the original record of the ld AO/ADM, the appellant was afforded an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under Section 46(4) of FSS Act for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory (in short "RFL"), if so desired, but the said option was not exercised.
Accordingly, a complaint was filed for taking action against the appellant.

Notice was issued by the Ld. AO to the appellant and it is borne out from the original record produced before this Court that appearance was put by Sh. Shailesh, AR of Smt. Bhavana Gupta on 09.08.2021 as well as 23.08.2021 in terms of the authority letter issued by the FBO, and on latter date, a reply was filed in which she pleaded guilty and requested for taking a lenient view.

The AR of the appellant then appeared on 06.09.2021, on which date, the matter was reserved for orders and eventually, the impugned order was passed on 19.04.2022.
4.
It is the case of the appellant that she received the copy of the impugned order on 06.05.2022 and then the present appeal was instituted on 26.07.2022.

Surprisingly, although the appellant admits that she is the sole proprietor of M/s Bankey Bihari Dairy in question, she has given an altogether different version of the story alleging that some person visited her shop on 16.01.2020 and purchased open ghee from her without disclosing his identity and it was later on that the FSO identified himself and intimidated her and her staff and forced them to sign certain blank documents and she only received communication from the Ld. AO/ADM for appearance on Smt. Bhavna Gupta vs The State on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65674291/
2 26.07.2021 and later appeared on 09.08.2021 and then on 23.08.2021 and she was shocked to receive the impugned order dated 19.04.2022 holding the appellant guilty and imposing penalty of Rs. One Lakh.

GROUNDS OF APPEAL:
5.

On the filing of the instant appeal, the operation of the impugned order was stayed subject to the appellant depositing 50% of the amount of the fine/penalty by way of DD/FDR/Bank Guarantee in the name of the court but the said order has not been complied with despite opportunities granted on 20.10.2022, 13.12.2022, 10.03.2023 and thereafter, arguments were advanced on the last date of hearing giving opportunity to the parties to file written submission but no one has preferred to file the same.
DECISION:
7. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the record of the present case, half hearted submissions made by the Ld. counsel for the appellant as also submissions made by the Ld. Chief PP for the State.
I have also perused the original record of the Ld. AO/ADM (Central).
8. At the outset, the instant appeal is bereft of any merits.

The term 'misbranded' or misbranded food' is defined by Section 3(1) (zf) (C) (i) of the FSS Act which means a food item which is packaged without "declaratory label" or is not labelled in accordance with requirement of this Act and Regulations thereunder.

Regulation 2.2.1 of the FSS (P&L) Regulation categorically stipulates the requirement of labelling of food item, which must contain certain declarations either in English or in Hindi Devnagri script and the label is stipulated to be clear, prominent, indelible and readily legible besides having license number of 'fssai'.
Regulation
) FSS (P&L) Regulation stipulates that every package of Vegetarian food shall bear a declaration on the label to the effect of the symbol and colour code which is "green colour filled circle".
Regulation 2.2.2.6 then stipulates that the name and complete address of the manufacturer and manufacturing unit shall be displayed on the label.
Regulation 2.2.2.7 mandates a declaration on the label with regard to net quantity or weight or volume or number as the case may be on the food item.

Regulation 2.2.2.8 Smt. Bhavna Gupta vs The State on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65674291/
3 mandates that label should be containing batch number or code number, or the lot number and likewise date of manufacture or packing.

entities.text: Regulation 2.2.2.8 Smt. Bhavna Gupta vs The State
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text:
Regulation 2.2.2.10 stipulates that the label should be containing "best before" and "use by date declaration".
9.
In the instant case all the aforesaid regulations were totally missing when the food item was being sold for human consumption.

It goes without saying that the appellant during the proceeding before the Ld. AO/ADM submitted a signed letter admitting her guilt as well and yet in the present appeal she has done a somersault and has denied all the allegations, which clearly amounts to perjury, and therefore,
although the quantum of penalty imposed appears to be little onerous, I am not interfering with the same.

10. In view of the foregoing discussions, the present appeal is dismissed and the impugned order purportedly passed under Section 52 of the FSS Act dated 19.04.2022 by the Ld. AO/ADM is upheld and the respondent shall be at liberty to execute the order for recovery of penalty amount.
The Record of the AO/ADM be returned along with the copy of the Judgment.
File of appeal be consigned to the Record Room.
DHARMESH SHARMA by DHARMESH SHARMA
